did_you_know.text: The term makkēh-nefesh literally combines 'to strike' and 'life' — basically 'one who strikes a life' — and refers to a killing that was not intentional. Ancient societies commonly distinguished deliberate murder from accidental killing.

In the ancient Near East the city gate was more than an entrance — elders gathered there and handled public and legal matters. That’s why the fleeing person stood at the gate and announced his case to the community.

The cities Bezer, Ramoth and Golan were set up east of the Jordan so people on that side could also find refuge. In effect there were three refuge cities on each side of the Jordan, spread out to provide access across the land.
